title: L2 Capstone: Mini Role-Playing Game
story: The final challenge. You've mastered data modeling across 59 lessons. Now build a tiny RPG battle system. A hero with a name, hit points, and gold faces off against monsters (Goblin, Skeleton, Dragon). The hero can Attack, Defend, or Use an Item. Simulate a battle and see who wins!
why: This capstone combines structs, enums, methods, matching, and mutation into a complete mini-game.
analogy: This RPG is like a tiny play. The Hero is the actor on stage. The Monster is the antagonist. Actions are the lines the actor chooses: "I attack!" "I defend!" "I drink a potion!" The battle function is the director — it reads the line, checks the actor's HP, and narrates the result. Every video game you've ever played builds on this same foundation.
try_it: Add a `Hero.is_alive(self) -> Bool` method that returns true if HP > 0. Add a `Troll` monster with 12 power and 40 gold. Add a `Flee` action that has a 50% chance to escape. Add critical hits: Attack has a 20% chance to do double damage. Simulate a full battle against a Dragon using multiple actions.
tips: Build the battle one step at a time: hero struct, monster enum, power method, damage, then the battle function
Use `var` for the hero so you can mutate HP and gold during battle
The `battle` function takes a `Hero` parameter — mutations inside the function affect the caller's hero
Use `if hp < 0 { hp = 0; }` to prevent negative HP after taking damage
common_mistakes: Forgetting `var` on the hero — without it, take_damage and healing won't persist between function calls
Not clamping HP to 0 in `take_damage` — negative HP can cause confusing displays
Missing match arms in `battle` — every Action variant must be handled
